newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria seeks compensation from Enel on LNG deal.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria seeks compensation from Enel on LNG deal.

text.p: Nigeria on Tuesday criticised the decision of Italian state power utility Enel to cancel a long-term contract to buy Nigerian Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) and said it was seeking compensation for the action.

"NLNG regrets Enel's conduct," the Nigerian LNG company (NLNG) said in a statement, adding "NLNG has initiated proceedings in Switzerland to obtain compensation from Enel for all losses resulting from Enel's breach of contract."

Enel said earlier that the decision to break the contract was linked to its abandonment of a project to construct a gas plant at Montalto di Castro, north of Rome, for economic, technical and environmental reasons.
Enel signed the contract in November and were to receive the first cargo of Nigerian LNG in the third quarter of 1999.

Nigeria's $4 billion LNG project plans to produce 7.2 billion cubic metres of LNG per year from a plant projected to start production in 1999. Enel was to take 3.5 billion cubic metres of the output annually.
NLNG said the compensation was yet to be quantified but was likely to be substantial.
"The value of the contract is estimated over its 22.5 years life to be at least $12 billion," it said.
Partners in the project are the Nigerian National Petroleum Corp, Shell Gas BV, Elf Aquitaine and Italy's Agip SpA.
Long-term supply contracts have been signed with Enargas of Spain and Gaz de France.
NLNG said the project would go ahead and sales to the other buyers would not be affected.
